+- Latest v0.2.20 instruction supersedes the old16→24 restoration and patchy-terrain choices below: the user explicitly requests genuinely more native WORLD pixels, detailed faces and equipment, redrawn gait keys and smoother movement. Native32×32 humanoids are authorized, guided by supplied sprites; keep originals and the16px movement/collision/save grid. Do not enlarge already reduced16px silhouettes and call that new detail. Native24 creatures remain supported alongside native32 bodies.
+- The user explicitly approves the v19 BOAR world sprite. Preserve all its packet/mask/attribute bytes and appearance. Keep the approved Kolkar, class master busts, welcome art, buildings and existing gameplay.
+- For v20 terrain the user permits either the dense texture or the plain ochre reference, but explicitly rejects mixing them. The chosen plain ochre treatment applies consistently to fields, paths and transparent ground beneath props. Preserve opaque supplied prop pixels, path colors/borders and collision bytes.
+- Generated world illustrations are authorized design sources for this redraw, not recovered native grids. Record direct32px lossy conversion separately from native authored animation keys; review actual LCD output from the final ROM.
+- Interrupt animation code must not `farcall`: it would overwrite foreground `hTempBank`/`wFarCallBC`. Keep the fire guard local and preserve the `BC` stack pointer, destination and WRAM bank. Native HDMA requests encode blocks minus one and wait for completion; never clear bit7 of an inactive `$ff` status, which starts another128-block GDMA.

Use the supplied decor PNGs as the active sources; keep their complete silhouettes. If a native budget blocks an exact import, report the measured limit rather than inventing simpler art.
 - The user prefers the earliest readable Peon, Boar and Imp character models over the v0.2.12 conversions. Restoring those archived native actor assets is explicitly authorized; retain the current approved buildings, interiors and working quest/gameplay code. Do not run their old broad generators.
 - On 2026-10-14 the user requested matching Shaman head/body proportions and quieter terrain with texture only in patches. Keep those changes in derived native packets; preserve supplied props, pillars, structures, palettes, collisions and warps. Sparse ground grains must come from the supplied dirt PNG, not newly drawn shapes.

engine/gfx/dma_transfer.asm.allowed_scope: Encode the exact requested HDMA block count and wait for hardware completion without writing its status register; prevent a completed transfer from restarting a spurious128-block GDMA at CGB double speed.
engine/gfx/dma_transfer.asm.diff:
diff --git a/engine/gfx/dma_transfer.asm b/engine/gfx/dma_transfer.asm
index 62cc02d2..8e659ae0 100644
--- a/engine/gfx/dma_transfer.asm
+++ b/engine/gfx/dma_transfer.asm
@@ -291,9 +291,10 @@ HDMATransfer_NoDI:
 	ld a, e
 	and $f0
 	ldh [rVDMA_DEST_LOW], a
-	; b = c | %10000000
-	ld a, c
+	; HDMA encodes blocks minus one. Request exactly C blocks, including
+	; at double CPU speed where the old extra block could finish early.
 	dec c
+	ld a, c
 	or $80
 	ld b, a
 	; d = $7f - c + 1
@@ -323,8 +324,13 @@ HDMATransfer_NoDI:
 	ld a, [hl]
 	dec c
 	jr nz, .loop3
-	ld hl, rVDMA_LEN
-	res 7, [hl]
+	; The exact request completes on its own. Never clear HDMA5 here: an
+	; inactive $ff would restart128-block GDMA; a read/clear/write also races
+	; the last HBlank. The reserved scanline window contains every block.
+.wait_hdma_complete
+	ldh a, [rVDMA_LEN]
+	bit 7, a
+	jr z, .wait_hdma_complete
 	ret
 
 HDMATransfer_WaitForScanline124:
@@ -348,9 +354,9 @@ _continue_HDMATransfer:
 	ld a, e
 	and $f0 ; high nybble
 	ldh [rVDMA_DEST_LOW], a
-	; e = c | %10000000
-	ld a, c
+	; E is the exact C-block request encoded as (C - 1) | $80.
 	dec c
+	ld a, c
 	or $80
 	ld e, a
 	; d = b - c + 1
@@ -387,8 +393,10 @@ _continue_HDMATransfer:
 	ld a, [hl]
 	dec c
 	jr nz, .final_ly_loop
-	ld hl, rVDMA_LEN
-	res 7, [hl]
+.wait_hdma_complete
+	ldh a, [rVDMA_LEN]
+	bit 7, a
+	jr z, .wait_hdma_complete
 	ei
 
 	ret

engine/tilesets/tileset_anims.asm.diff:
diff --git a/engine/tilesets/tileset_anims.asm b/engine/tilesets/tileset_anims.asm
index 53a85497..ff8b97e1 100644
--- a/engine/tilesets/tileset_anims.asm
+++ b/engine/tilesets/tileset_anims.asm
@@ -71,16 +71,78 @@ rept 6
 	add a
 endr
 	add e
+	if !DEF(PEON_ENVIRONMENT_TEST)
+	; This executes inside VBlank. Never farcall here: ReturnFarCall uses
+	; foreground scratch (wFarCallBC), so an interrupt would corrupt BC and
+	; potentially the caller's saved stack pointer. The local guard preserves
+	; BC/DE, the ROM bank and WRAM bank without touching that shared scratch.
+	push af
+	call PeonFireUsesUniformGroundV0220
+	jr c, .uniform_ground
+	pop af
+	endc
 	add LOW(PeonEnvironmentFireFrames)
 	ld l, a
 	ld a, 0
 	adc HIGH(PeonEnvironmentFireFrames)
 	ld h, a
+	if !DEF(PEON_ENVIRONMENT_TEST)
+	jr .write
+.uniform_ground
+	pop af
+	add LOW(PeonUniformEnvironmentFireFramesV0220)
+	ld l, a
+	ld a, 0
+	adc HIGH(PeonUniformEnvironmentFireFramesV0220)
+	ld h, a
+.write
+	endc
 	ld sp, hl
 	ld h, d
 	ld l, e
 	jp WriteTile
 
+IF !DEF(PEON_ENVIRONMENT_TEST)
+; Same thirteen exterior map IDs as PeonUsesExtendedNativeEnvironmentV0213.
+; Map headers are read in WRAM1 even when the interrupt arrived in a cache
+; bank. No ROM switch, farcall, temporary global or DE/HL mutation is needed.
+PeonFireUsesUniformGroundV0220:
+	push bc
+	ldh a, [rWBK]
+	ld c, a
+	ld a, BANK(wMapTileset)
+	ldh [rWBK], a
+	ld a, [wMapTileset]
+	cp TILESET_PEON
+	jr nz, .no
+	ld a, [wMapGroup]
+	cp GROUP_PEON_OPENING
+	jr nz, .no
+	ld a, [wMapNumber]
+	cp MAP_PEON_OPENING
+	jr z, .yes
+	cp MAP_THE_DEN
+	jr c, .no
+	cp MAP_BURNING_BLADE_CAVERN + 1
+	jr c, .yes
+	cp MAP_PEON_VALLEY_CROSSROADS
+	jr c, .no
+	cp MAP_PEON_VALLEY_EXIT + 1
+	jr nc, .no
+.yes
+	ld a, c
+	ldh [rWBK], a
+	pop bc
+	scf
+	ret
+.no
+	ld a, c
+	ldh [rWBK], a
+	pop bc
+	and a
+	ret
+ENDC
+
 PeonEnvironmentFireFrames:
 	if DEF(PEON_ENVIRONMENT_TEST)
 	INCBIN "gfx/tilesets/peon_environment_v2/fire_frames.bin"
@@ -89,6 +151,11 @@ PeonEnvironmentFireFrames:
